topic: Breath series 3: Box breathing (animated, promotes the app)
caption:
Box breathing may work best before the hard moment, not during it.

Box breathing has four equal sides: in for four, hold for four, out for four, hold for four. In a recent study, university students used one minute of it in real moments of everyday anxiety and felt less anxious five minutes later than when they carried on as usual, about as much as with cyclic sighing. They rated box breathing the easier of the two. In a lab study, people doing box breathing during a demanding task had calmer bodies but were slower at the task than with a simple long breath out, so the researchers suggest it may suit moments when you can pause.

How to try it: one round of in, hold, out, hold, four seconds each. If a hold feels uncomfortable, shorten it, and lower all four counts together. If you have a heart, lung or blood condition, epilepsy, or are pregnant, check with your doctor before using breath holds. These were small studies, mostly with young, healthy adults.

The free guided breathing in our Tools and Courses app can keep the count for you. Find it in our profile links.

Save this for later.
